faq: Do I need to prepare anything?
Just a rough list of what takes up your week and who does it. We send a short question sheet before the interview, and fifteen minutes of preparation is plenty.
Will you tell me to buy specific products?
We name tools that fit each idea, but we are not paid by any tool maker and we often suggest free options or features you already own. The advice is independent.
Will the time savings be exact?
No. We give honest estimates based on what you tell us and typical results, shown as ranges. Real savings depend on how your team adopts the change.
Can you also build what the audit suggests?
Yes, if you want. The audit stands on its own and can be used by anyone. If you choose us for a build, we quote it separately from the audit findings.

desc:
An AI opportunity audit for small businesses finds where AI would genuinely help before you buy a tool. Ecom Swift LLC interviews you and your team, lists the tasks that eat your week, and ranks them by time saved, effort and risk.

## What is an AI opportunity audit?

An AI opportunity audit is a structured review of how your business runs day to day, done to find the tasks where AI could save the most time or effort. It starts with people and tasks, not products. The result is a ranked list in plain words, so you know what to try first and what to leave alone.

Think of it as a map made before the journey. It does not install anything. It tells you where installing something would pay off.

## Why start with an audit and not a tool

Most owners begin by hearing about a tool and then looking for a place to use it. That order produces odd purchases. You may end up with a clever writing assistant while the real drain is manual copying between spreadsheets, or repeated answers to the same five customer questions.

An audit reverses the order. It asks where your hours go, which tasks repeat, where errors creep in and which jobs people dread. Only then does it ask whether AI is the right answer, and sometimes the honest answer is a simple template, a checklist or a change in process.

## How ranking tasks improves your results

Ranking brings focus, and focus saves money. Each task is scored on the time it could save, the effort to set it up and the risk if the tool gets something wrong. A task that takes hours each week, follows the same pattern every time and carries little risk rises to the top. A task that is rare, delicate or full of exceptions falls to the bottom.

This scoring protects you from two common errors: starting with the hardest problem, and starting with the most exciting one. The first small wins also build the confidence your team needs for bigger changes later. Exact savings depend on how work is really done, so we describe them as estimates and not promises.

## What a strong audit includes

- Interviews with the people who actually do the work, not only the owner.
- A full list of recurring tasks, written in everyday words.
- A time estimate for each task, based on what people tell us.
- A score for time saved, effort to set up and risk.
- A ranked shortlist with a short paragraph on each top idea.
- Notes on which kinds of tools fit each idea, in general terms.
- Cost notes where the report calls for them.
- A clear do now, do later and skip grouping.
- Risk comments covering customer data and quality checks.

## How we carry out the audit

We begin with a conversation. In the Basic package that is one interview with you, covering up to a set number of tasks. Standard extends this to several people on one team and adds scores for each task. Premium interviews more people across the business and ends with a written action plan and a results call.

After the interviews we group similar tasks, score them and write the report. Each top idea is explained in a short paragraph: what the task is, why it ranks where it does and what a first small step could look like. Add-ons include extra team interviews, a one page summary of your top priorities and a follow-up call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe tasks as they really happen, including the awkward workarounds.
- Let team members speak for themselves, since they know the details.
- Mention tasks you dislike, because those are often good candidates.
- Be honest about what customer information is involved.
- Start with the top two or three ideas, not the whole list.

**Avoid:**
- Choosing a tool before the audit is finished.
- Hiding tasks because they seem too small to matter.
- Expecting every task to be a good fit for AI.
- Starting with a task where one mistake would be costly.
- Treating the ranked list as permanent when your business changes.

## Who this is for

This audit suits an owner of a growing shop who spends evenings on admin and cannot tell which tool to try. It suits a manager of a small agency whose team repeats similar emails, reports and notes all week. It also suits a founder who has been given a budget for AI and needs a defensible starting point.

## What we need from you

Little preparation is needed. Tell us about your business, the roles in your team and the time slots that suit the interviews. If you have a list of tasks, a process document or example files, send them, but this is optional. We never ask for passwords or account access to run the audit, because the work is built on conversation. If an interview benefits from seeing a screen, you can share it live.
